chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The sweet pomegranate was mentioned, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Muzz is corrective in the belly.'

key_terms.الْمُزُّ: A specific variety of pomegranate, often described as sweet or soft

ai.seo_question: What type of pomegranate is considered best for the stomach according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies 'Al-Muzz' as the superior variety of pomegranate for digestive health, reflecting the Shia tradition's emphasis on practical medicine (al-Tibb) derived from the Imams. This narration underscores the holistic view of nutrition in Shia jurisprudence, where specific food attributes are linked to bodily well-being and spiritual purity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Al Waleed Bin Sabeeh,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘The sweet Pomegranate was mentioned, so heasws said: ‘Al-Muzz (a type of Pomegranate) is corrective in the belly’.
en.sarwar: 14. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from al-Walid ibn Sabih who has said the following:

“Once sweet pomegranate was mentioned and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Sour-sweet pomegranate is more suitable for the stomach.’” Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘ Abd al-Hamid from al-Walid ibn Sabih from abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated from a similar Hadith.”
